name: AI, Machine Learning & Robotics
description: Artificial intelligence from first contact to the research frontier: classical AI (search, logic, planning), probabilistic reasoning, machine learning, deep learning, reinforcement learning, language, speech and vision, LLMs and generative AI, data science and MLOps, plus robotics from kinematics and control to mobile, legged, aerial, humanoid and wearable robots.

chapters.name: Introduction to AI & Machine Learning
chapters.summary: A gentle first tour of what AI and machine learning are, how machines learn from data, and where AI is used today, assuming only high-school maths.

topics.name: What is artificial intelligence? Definitions and everyday examples
A short history: from Turing and Dartmouth to deep learning and ChatGPT
How machines learn: data, features, models and predictions
Supervised, unsupervised and reinforcement learning in plain terms
A first model by hand: fitting a line and drawing a decision boundary
Training, testing and why models make mistakes (overfitting in pictures)
Neural networks and deep learning, intuitively
Generative AI and chatbots: what large language models do
Robots and embodied AI: sense, think, act
Hands-on without code: Teachable Machine, notebooks and chat assistants
Limits, bias and societal impact of AI
Careers and learning paths in AI, ML and robotics

chapters.name: Core AI Concepts
chapters.summary: The big ideas behind AI: intelligent agents, narrow versus general AI, the history and philosophy of the field, and the symbolic and connectionist paradigms.

topics.name: Intelligent agents and environments (PEAS, agent types, rationality)
Major milestones: Dartmouth, expert systems, AI winters, deep learning, LLMs

chapters.name: Programming & Tools for Data Science

chapters.name: Mathematics & Statistics for Data Science
chapters.summary: A practitioner's survey of the linear algebra, calculus, probability and statistics used every day in data science and machine learning.

topics.name: Problem formulation: states, actions, goal tests and path costs
